- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 39a78b151d691a538856c0f0d57304f8faa69f96` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b4fc36f35e265f6c25471504842838d88f58fe2a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/upsert-conflict-clause.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-upsert-empty-merge-set.test.ts + .changeset/8740-upsert-nothing-to-merge.md (prose face, read for ②), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts (`PhysicalIndex`, `introspectIndexes`: partial and expression key parts), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/live-dialect-matrix.testkit.ts (cell declaration, skip-vs-fail rule), packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts (`isUniqueViolationError`), packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts and packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts (the PR body's claim about the remote twin), .github/workflows/ci.yml (the `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job's `if:`), docs/adr/0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md

Inputs: card #8740 (body and every comment, the seat's ruling B in the round-2 dev report included), PR #26015 body, file list and the net diff `origin/main...b4fc36f3` (4 files, +389/-26), and the 54 check-runs on the head. Disclosure rule of the card observed: this record describes the change in abstract terms only.

### ① Derived judgments

Read of the diff. `withUpsertConflictClause` (new, not exported from `index.ts`) returns the bare insertion when `columnsToMerge` is empty and `onConflict(mergeKeys).merge(columnsToMerge)` otherwise; the bare `merge()` fallback is gone from `upsert`. On the empty path `assertConflictTargetBackedWithoutClause` runs before the statement on every dialect, reading the same cached `introspectKeyIndexes` the MySQL pre-flight reads, with the pre-flight's certainty rule (failed read or no keys at all: proceed; a refusal is preceded by a fresh re-read) and the pre-flight's cover predicate, both now shared helpers (`indexCoversConflictTarget`, `unbackedConflictTargetCause`). The in-statement scope predicate is applied only when the statement has a merge leg.

1. **Collision on the empty-merge path, backed target: merge-every-column becomes a unique violation and no column is rewritten.** RIGHT, and the card's ruled shape. This is the narrowing the changeset declares. The MySQL after-statement fence and the #8807 identity check still run on that path and are satisfied by the inserted row (read back by `id`); a collision throws before either, inside the same unit of work. The read-back of a non-colliding call is unchanged (target absent from the payload, so it reads by `id`, as before).

2. **Unbacked target on the empty-merge path, table carrying at least one PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index: refused `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 on all three dialects, nothing written.** RIGHT (seat ruling B). On SQLite and PostgreSQL the refusal's `cause` is now the introspection sentence (schema identifiers only) where it used to be the server's own sentence; message, code and status are the shared wording. Judged a diagnostic-only change.

3. **Unbacked target on the empty-merge path, table with NO key at all, or an introspection read that fails: the plain INSERT proceeds.** This is a WIDENING on SQLite and PostgreSQL that the diff implies and no text names: with a conflict clause the server refused the call (no arbiter index) and the driver answered `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400; now the uncertain-answer legs of the pre-flight's certainty rule let the statement run, and on a keyless table it inserts. On MySQL the same call already proceeded (the pre-flight has always let it through, and `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` on a keyless table inserts), so MySQL is unchanged. Judged ACCEPTABLE as behaviour: the rule exists because an empty catalog answer is indistinguishable from a mistyped table name, and nothing can collide on a keyless table so nothing is overwritten. Judged WRONG as public text: the changeset sentence "A conflict target that no PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index backs is still refused on that path" is unqualified, and the PR body's Acceptance note repeats it. See ③ for the action.

4. **A target the caller did NOT name is not exempt from the no-clause refusal.** `assertConflictTargetHonoured` returns without refusing when `callerNamed` is false (#8807: the driver's own `['id']` default is never refused); `assertConflictTargetBackedWithoutClause` takes no such argument. The default target reaches the empty path only when `id` is absent from `formatted`, which `applyWriteColumnMap` can do for an external object whose `columnMap` remaps `id`. On that shape (default target, payload of insert-only columns only, remapped `id`) the pre-fix statement already failed on SQLite and PostgreSQL (the conflict clause named a column the table does not have) and merged every column on MySQL; now all three refuse before the statement, with no collision needed. Judged a divergence from the #8807 rule on a degenerate shape, not a defect in the ruling: naming it here so the seat decides whether to thread `callerNamed` through (passing it would skip the check and let the plain INSERT answer, which loses nothing). See ③.

5. **A scope-fenced collision on the empty-merge path.** Before and after, the call is refused and writes nothing; the error envelope moves from the driver's fence refusal to the dialect's own unique-violation error, the same error a `create()` collision already raises on these tables. Judged RIGHT, no new surface.

6. **Everything with a column to merge, or with the target in the payload, is byte-identical.** RIGHT: the compile pins in the new test show the clause and the exact merged column on all three clients, and `noopMergeColumns` is untouched (#8622's reachable no-op stays).

7. **Seat question (b), the shared cover helper.** Exact set equality over the index's columns, order-insensitive, which is how both `ON CONFLICT` dialects infer an arbiter and the only reading a composite key admits: RIGHT. Absent cache: a read is made and cached; failed read (`null`) and empty key set: proceed; a refusal is preceded by a fresh read: all RIGHT and identical to the pre-flight (the helper is the pre-flight's own `covers`, now hoisted). Partial indexes are filtered out of the key set by `introspectKeyIndexes` (`partial !== true`), so a target backed only by a partial unique index reads as unbacked, which is what the server with a clause answered too: RIGHT. Expression key parts: an attributable part lands in `columns`, an unattributable one is omitted from `columns`, so an index over (col, expr) can read as covering (col); the error direction is "proceed", the safe one under the certainty rule, and it is the pre-flight's existing reading: RIGHT. Case and quoting: identifiers are compared verbatim against the target as emitted (knex quotes the conflict target; the write column map is applied to the row, never to the target), the pre-flight's documented rule: RIGHT. Scope column: matched like any column when a target names it, and the scope fencing on the no-merge statement was read against each dialect: RIGHT (detail kept off this public record under the card's disclosure rule).

8. **Seat question (c), public text.** PR body, changeset, test file header and titles, code comments, the shared `cause` text and the new helper's doc read in full. None names a reproduction or a path to one; the vocabulary ("insert-only columns", "merge-ALL", "a collision is refused and rewrites nothing") is the card body's own, public since 2026-08-14, and the 17.6.0 changelog already names the insert-only set. The round-2 dev report on the card says only that step 1 was measured and held. NEUTRAL. The only text defect is accuracy, not disclosure (item 3).

9. **ADR-0112 assertion shape.** The unbacked-target cell asserts `code === 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` and `status === 400`, both, on every dialect cell. The two unique-violation cells assert `isUniqueViolationError` plus the dialect's native code; a server error carries no declared status (ADR-0112's status-channel note: the door derives it), so there is no status to assert there. RIGHT. The cells also assert the stored rows and `created_at` unchanged, which is the pin the card asked for.

10. **The PR body's claim about `driver-turso`.** Its remote transport emits `DO NOTHING` on an empty merge set (remote-transport.ts, its own statement builder) and its local face returns `super.upsert` (turso-driver.ts), so the twin is untouched and inherits this change on the local face only. RIGHT.

11. **Test placement.** `sql-driver-upsert-empty-merge-set.test.ts` sits in `src/` and imports the driver as `../src/index.js`, the style 117 sibling tests in that directory use. The live cells are declared through `declareDialectCell`, which names a missing URL as a skip and makes it fatal under `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`. RIGHT.

Check-runs on the head, as they stood when read: 54 runs; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (8 shards), `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, the three single-writer and card-claim guards, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check Documentation Links`: all success. `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` skipped, by its own `if:` (`github.event_name != 'pull_request'`): the live PostgreSQL and MySQL cells of the new file have not run in CI on this head. UI and docs lanes skipped (no path). No failure.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/driver-sql` patch with a BREAKING banner, declared a served-set narrowing. Matches what the diff publishes: no exported symbol, type or schema changes (`upsert-conflict-clause.ts` is not exported; `index.ts` is untouched), no metadata key moves (ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right), and the only accept-set move the diff intends is a collision that used to merge now being refused. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the changeset and on the PR body, consistent with each other and with the round-2 dev report; the dispatch claim's expected `yes` was superseded by measurement, as the report says. Item 3 above is the one place the changeset's prose is wider than the diff: the unbacked-target sentence needs the qualifier "on a table that carries at least one PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE index; a table with none, or one whose keys cannot be read, proceeds to the plain INSERT, as the MySQL pre-flight always has". The level itself is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (unbacked target on the empty-merge path, options A/B): seat ruled B; implemented on this head as described; pinned per dialect cell with code and status. ANSWERED. Residue: items 3 and 4 above, which B's wording ("the cached physical key indexes", "the existing refusal") did not reach.
- Dev flag, round-2 report: the MySQL cell ran locally against MariaDB 10.11.14, not MySQL 8; the PR body says the MySQL 8 pin runs in `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`. That job is push-only by design and is skipped on this head, so the live cells are unmeasured in CI until the merge lands on `main`. ESCALATED to the seat: read that job's run on the merge commit before closing the card; if it is red on the new file, the card reopens.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope finding 1 (dogfood `authz-probe-blind-spot.test.ts` red on `main` after #25956): not this diff; `packages/runtime` untouched. ANSWERED as main-red, the seat's to route.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope finding 2 (`isUniqueViolationError` matches a non-unique MySQL error whose message echoes a statement): not this diff; the new tests pin the native code beside the predicate for that reason. ANSWERED as out of scope; worth its own card.
- Docs drift advisory on the PR: 9 hand-written pages name `SqlDriver` as a symbol; none documents the upsert merge set or the conflict clause (read: `data-modeling/drivers.mdx` names the class only). No doc edit owed by this PR.
- Seat action 1 (from item 3): the changeset and the PR body's first Acceptance note overstate the refusal. Either amend the changeset sentence with the qualifier in ② on a follow-up commit (a new head, which needs a fresh record) or record the qualification on the card when closing it. The seat decides; this record's PASS covers the code and the level, not that sentence.
- Seat action 2 (from item 4): decide whether `assertConflictTargetBackedWithoutClause` should take the pre-flight's `callerNamed` exemption. Not blocking: the only reachable shape is an external object whose `columnMap` remaps `id`, where the pre-fix call already failed on two dialects.
- Scope breach: none. `packages/spec/**` untouched; file surface `packages/drivers/driver-sql/**` plus one changeset, as claimed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-slwx8p`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**
